# Mia Tool Spec

The tool registry architecture is defined in `docs/tool-registry-redesign.md`; this
file specifies each tool. Tools are implemented against the `Tool` trait in
`src/agent_tools/` and registered in `ToolRegistry::init()`.

## Conventions

- **Naming:** `fs_*` filesystem, `doc_*` documents, `web_*` web, `exec_*` execution.
  Every `fs_*` tool is `fs_<verb>_<object>` (e.g. `fs_read_file`, not `fs_readfile`).
- **Permission classes:** `readonly` never prompts; `write` prompts, side effects
  limited to a single file; `execute` prompts, arbitrary side effects.
- **Errors:** all tools return `(ToolStatus, payload)` via the `ok()` / `err()`
  helpers in `agent_tools.rs`. No panics on model/API-controlled input —
  malformed args, missing files, failed spawns are `err(...)`.
- **LLM payload:** every success payload carries `"status": "success"`; every error
  carries `{"status": "error", "message": ...}` (built by `err()`).
- **TUI output:** tools may additionally push user-facing output to the TUI via
  `ctx.handle.tool_output(...)`; that is presentation only, the JSON payload is what
  the LLM consumes.
- **Shared helpers:** `ok()`/`err()`; a process-wide static `reqwest::Client` for
  network tools; cached `SyntaxSet`/`ThemeSet` behind syntax highlighting for
  permission prompts.
- **Availability:** probed live; a tool is hidden from the LLM when unavailable.

# Tools

## datetime
- **Permission:** readonly
- **Description:** Fetch the current date and time (RFC 2822) plus unix epoch.
  Use whenever precise time is required (e.g. before web searches that mention
  "current year" or "latest version").
- **Args:** none.
- **Returns:**
  ```json
  { "status": "success", "datetime": "Fri, 16 Oct 2026 17:29:00 +0530", "epoch": 1790000000 }
  ```
- **Notes:** trivially simple; the reference implementation for the new Tool trait.

---

## fs_read_file
- **Permission:** readonly
- **Description:** Read any text or document-class file. Text files (txt, rtf, csv,
  any source-code file by extension) are read as-is; document files (odt, ods, odp,
  doc, docx, xls, xlsx, ppt, pptx, pdf) are converted to text first (via xberg).
- **Args:**
  - `path` (required, string): file to read. Tilde-expanded.
  - `offset` (optional, integer, default 0): character offset to start reading from.
  - `max_chars` (optional, integer, default 10000, max 100000): characters to read.
- **Returns:**
  ```json
  {
    "status": "success",
    "path": "src/main.rs",
    "converted": false,
    "contents": "…up to max_chars chars…",
    "total_len": 48231,
    "next_offset": 10000,
    "is_truncated": true
  }
  ```
  - `converted`: `true` when the content passed through xberg.
  - `next_offset`: character offset for the next chunk, or `null` when `contents`
    reaches the end of the file (`offset + contents.len() >= total_len`).
  - `is_truncated`: `true` when more content remains after this chunk.
- **Notes:** offsets are in **characters**, not bytes (UTF-8). v1 reads the whole
  file into memory then slices — O(n) per chunked call, acceptable. Non-UTF-8 /
  binary input falls back to xberg conversion; if that also fails, `err(...)`.
  Because `converted` documents are re-converted per chunk, conversion output is
  non-deterministic across chunks — acceptable, documented.

---

## fs_write_file
- **Permission:** write
- **Description:** Write text content to a UTF-8 file, fully overwriting it if it
  exists. Cannot create documents (see `doc_create`). Use for new files and full
  rewrites; prefer `fs_edit_file` for targeted changes to existing files.
- **Args:**
  - `path` (required, string): destination. Tilde-expanded.
  - `content` (required, string): full new content.
  - `create_parents` (optional, boolean, default true): create missing parent
    directories (`mkdir -p` semantics).
- **Returns:** `{ "status": "success", "path": "...", "size": 1234 }`
- **Notes:** permission prompt shows the content with syntax highlighting (via
  `permission_prompt`).

## fs_search_files
- **Permission:** readonly
- **Description:** Search file **contents** recursively (ripgrep under the hood).
  Respects `.gitignore`, skips hidden files by default, smart-case by default.
- **Args:**
  - `pattern` (required, string): regex to search for (or literal with
    `fixed_strings`).
  - `path` (optional, string, default "."): root to search. Tilde-expanded.
  - `max_depth` (required, integer): recursion limit — forces the model to scope
    the search deliberately.
  - `case_sensitive` (optional, boolean, default false): when false, smart-case
    matching (case-sensitive only when the pattern contains uppercase). Maps to
    `-s`.
  - `fixed_strings` (optional, boolean, default false): treat the pattern as a
    literal string, not regex. Use when the search string contains regex
    metacharacters (`foo.bar`, `a+b`, `C:\path`). Maps to `-F`.
  - `word_regexp` (optional, boolean, default false): match whole words only.
    Maps to `-w`.
  - `files_with_matches` (optional, boolean, default false): return only the
    files that contain a match, no lines. Maps to `-l`.
  - `count_only` (optional, boolean, default false): return per-file match counts
    instead of individual lines. Maps to `-c`.
  - `include_globs` (optional, array of strings): only search files matching
    these globs, e.g. `["*.rs"]`, `["src/**"]`. Maps to `-g 'glob'`.
  - `exclude_globs` (optional, array of strings): skip files matching these
    globs, e.g. `["tests/**", "*.lock"]`. Maps to `-g '!glob'`.
  - `hidden` (optional, boolean, default false): also search hidden files.
    Maps to `--hidden`.
  - `no_ignore` (optional, boolean, default false): also search gitignored files
    (build output, vendored deps, generated code). Maps to `--no-ignore`.
  - `context_lines` (optional, integer, default 0, max 20): include N lines of
    context before and after each match. Maps to `-C N`.
- **Returns:**
  - default mode:
    ```json
    {
      "status": "success",
      "count": 3,
      "matches": [ { "path": "src/main.rs", "line": 25, "text": "mod agent_tools;" } ]
    }
    ```
  - `files_with_matches: true`:
    ```json
    { "status": "success", "count": 2, "files": ["src/main.rs", "src/api.rs"] }
    ```
  - `count_only: true`:
    ```json
    { "status": "success", "count": 2, "counts": [ { "path": "src/main.rs", "count": 14 } ] }
    ```
  - `context_lines > 0`: each match gains `"context_before": [...]` and
    `"context_after": [...]` arrays (context lines trimmed of trailing
    whitespace).
- **Notes:** invokes the `rg` binary with the mapped flags (`--color=never`).
  Zero matches is **success** with `count: 0`, not an error (rg's exit code 1 is
  not a failure here). The ripgrep crates (`grep`, `ignore`, `grep-searcher`)
  exist as libs if the binary dependency is ever dropped — v1 uses the binary.

---

## fs_search_dirs
- **Permission:** readonly
- **Description:** Find files and directories **by name** (fd under the hood).
  Pattern is a regex by default; respects `.gitignore`, skips hidden by default.
- **Args:**
  - `pattern` (required, string): filename pattern.
  - `path` (optional, string, default "."): root to search. Tilde-expanded.
  - `max_depth` (required, integer): recursion limit.
  - `use_glob` (optional, boolean, default false): treat the pattern as a glob
    (`*.toml`, `test_*.py`, `{a,b}.rs`) instead of a regex. Maps to `-g`.
  - `fixed_strings` (optional, boolean, default false): treat the pattern as a
    literal string, not a regex. Maps to `-F`.
  - `case_sensitive` (optional, boolean, default false): fd matches
    case-insensitively by default; set `true` for exact case. Maps to `-s`.
  - `type` (optional, string): `"file" | "dir" | "symlink"` — restrict result
    kinds. Maps to `-t`.
  - `extension` (optional, string): only results with this extension, e.g. `"rs"`,
    `"toml"`. Maps to `-e`.
  - `hidden` (optional, boolean, default false): also search hidden files.
    Maps to `--hidden`.
  - `no_ignore` (optional, boolean, default false): also search gitignored paths.
    Maps to `--no-ignore`.
- **Returns:** `{ "status": "success", "count": 2, "matches": ["src/tui.rs", "src/tui/"] }`
- **Notes:** invokes the `fd` binary with the mapped flags
  (`--color=never --hyperlink=never`). Zero matches is success. fd has no official
  library; if the binary dependency is ever dropped, use the `ignore` crate's
  walker instead.

## fs_tree
- **Permission:** readonly
- **Description:** Display a directory tree. Used to cheaply grasp project
  structure without reading files.
- **Args:**
  - `path` (optional, string, default "."): root. Tilde-expanded.
  - `max_depth` (required, integer): recursion limit.
  - `show_hidden` (optional, boolean, default false).
- **Returns:**
  ```json
  { "status": "success", "tree": ".\n├── src\n│   ├── main.rs\n│   └── … (14 more entries)", "truncated": true, "depth_reached": 3 }
  ```
- **Notes:** `truncated: true` when a directory at `max_depth` has children — the
  tree shows `… (N more entries)` so the model never mistakes a truncated tree for
  the full structure. v1 implementation: `ignore::WalkBuilder` (respects
  `.gitignore`, hidden skip, max depth) rendered as a text tree.

## fs_list_dir
- **Permission:** readonly
- **Description:** Basic `ls -al`-style listing of a single directory.
- **Args:** `path` (optional, string, default "."). Tilde-expanded.
- **Returns:**
  ```json
  {
    "status": "success",
    "count": 3,
    "entries": [
      { "name": "src", "type": "dir", "permissions": "drwxr-xr-x", "size": "4.0 KiB", "owner": "mathew", "group": "users", "modified": "2026-10-16 17:00:00" }
    ]
  }
  ```
- **Notes:** directories first, then files, sorted by name. `permissions` is the
  `ls`-style rwx string (unix); owner/group via `uzers` on unix, `-` on windows.
  Structured JSON (not a table) so the model can reason about entries; optionally
  mirror a rendered table to the TUI via `tool_output`.

## fs_edit_file
- **Permission:** write
- **Description:** Apply targeted, context-matched edits to an existing UTF-8 text
  file **without rewriting it**. The replacement for the old "use sed/awk via
  exec_shell" pattern. Prefer over `fs_write_file` for modifying existing files.
- **Args:**
  - `path` (required, string): file to edit. Tilde-expanded. File must exist.
  - `edits` (required, array): `[ { "old_text": string, "new_text": string }, ... ]`
    — a batch of edits applied in one call (one permission prompt).
- **Returns:**
  ```json
  { "status": "success", "path": "src/main.rs", "edits_applied": 2, "message": "2 edits applied" }
  ```
- **Notes / algorithm:**
  1. File must exist and be valid UTF-8, else `err(...)`.
  2. Read content. For each edit (1-based index), against the **original** content:
     `count = content.matches(old_text).count()`.
  3. `count != 1` → **fail the whole batch** (no partial writes):
     `err("edit {i}: matched {count} times, need exactly 1 — refine old_text")`.
  4. Apply via `replacen(old_text, new_text, 1)` per edit.
  5. Write once (temp file + rename for atomicity). No partial application.
- **Permission prompt:** header `Edit {path}`; content shows the old/new blocks
  (a minimal diff), optionally highlighted.

---

## fs_file_ops
- **Permission:** write
- **Description:** Single-file filesystem operations: move/rename, copy, delete.
- **Args:**
  - `operation` (required, string): `"move" | "copy" | "delete"`.
  - `source` (required, string): source path. Tilde-expanded.
  - `destination` (optional, string): required for `move`/`copy`. Tilde-expanded.
  - `overwrite` (optional, boolean, default false): when false, error if
    `destination` already exists.
- **Returns:**
  ```json
  { "status": "success", "operation": "move", "source": "a.md", "destination": "docs/a.md", "size": 2048 }
  ```
- **Notes:**
  - `move`: `fs::rename`, with copy+remove fallback on cross-device (`EXDEV`).
  - `copy`: `fs::copy`.
  - `delete`: file only (`fs::remove_file`) — refuses directories; no recursive
    delete in v1. Deleting a symlink removes the link, not the target (state this
    in the schema description).
  - `move`/`copy` create missing parent directories of `destination`.
- **Permission prompt:** `Delete {source}` / `Move {source} → {destination}` /
  `Copy {source} → {destination}`.

## exec_shell
- **Permission:** execute
- **Description:** Execute a shell command (bash on Unix, PowerShell on Windows)
  and return stdout, stderr, exit code. Use for everything outside the specialized
  tools: builds, package managers, git, custom scripts.
- **Args:**
  - `command` (required, string): the command to run.
  - `working_dir` (optional, string): working directory (default: current).
  - `timeout_secs` (optional, integer, default 30, max 300): kill the child on
    timeout.
  - `use_nix_shell` (optional, boolean, default false): run the command inside a
    nix dev shell (`nix develop --command bash -c '<command>'`).
  - `nix_shell_path` (optional, string): path to the flake/shell to use; defaults
    to the current working directory's flake.
- **Returns:**
  ```json
  { "status": "success", "exit_code": 0, "stdout": "...", "stderr": "...", "timed_out": false }
  ```
- **Notes:**
  - v1 is **one-shot spawn per call** — no persistent shell (the session-shell
    architecture from the design spec is deferred; the Tool trait supports it later).
  - Async `tokio::process::Command`; stream partial output to the TUI via
    `ctx.handle.partial_tool_output`; kill child on timeout **and** on
    `ctx.handle.cancel` cancellation.
  - Spawn/wait failures are `err(...)`, never panics.
  - `availability()`: bash (Unix) / powershell (Windows) present.

---

## exec_python
- **Permission:** execute
- **Description:** Execute a Python 3 code snippet (a fresh interpreter per call —
  no state persists between calls). Use for scripting, math, and deterministic
  text processing.
- **Args:**
  - `code` (required, string): the snippet to run.
  - `working_dir` (optional, string): working directory (default: current).
  - `timeout_secs` (optional, integer, default 30, max 300).
- **Returns:**
  ```json
  { "status": "success", "exit_code": 0, "stdout": "...", "stderr": "...", "timed_out": false }
  ```
- **Notes:** same runner/shared helper as `exec_shell` (`python3 -c` on Unix,
  `python` on Windows). Permission prompt shows the code syntax-highlighted.
- **`availability()`:** python3 (Unix) / python (Windows) present.

---

## doc_create
- **Permission:** write
- **Description:** Create a brand-new document from markup (markdown, latex, or
  typst) into any output format (pdf, docx, odt, html, …). Use for new documents;
  use `doc_convert` when the source file already exists.
- **Args:**
  - `input_format` (required, string): `"markdown" | "latex" | "typst"`.
  - `contents` (required, string): the document source.
  - `output_file` (required, string): full output path; the extension determines
    the target format.
- **Returns:**
  ```json
  { "status": "success", "exit_code": 0, "stdout": "...", "stderr": "...", "output_path": "out.pdf" }
  ```
- **Notes:**
  - Writes `contents` to a temp input file, then invokes the engine.
  - `latex → pdf`: `pdflatex` with `-jobname` + `-output-directory` (the old code
    wrongly passed the output path as a positional argument to pdflatex — fixed).
    Re-run pdflatex twice for references (or use `latexmk` if present).
  - `typst → pdf`: `typst compile` (availability checked at call time, not
    registration, since it depends on the requested format).
  - everything else: `pandoc --from <input_format> -o <output_file>`.
  - Engine missing → `err(...)` with which engine is missing.
- **Permission prompt:** `Create {format} document` + `({bytes} bytes → {output})`.
- **`availability()`:** pandoc present (engines validated per call).

---

## doc_convert
- **Permission:** write
- **Description:** Convert an existing file from one format to another (pandoc).
  Also the read-side bridge: convert pdf/docx/etc. to markdown for reading.
- **Args:**
  - `input_path` (required, string): source file. Tilde-expanded.
  - `output_path` (required, string): destination; extension determines target
    format unless `to_format` is given. Tilde-expanded.
  - `from_format` (optional, string): override input format detection.
  - `to_format` (optional, string): override output format.
  - `extra_args` (optional, array of strings): allowlisted pandoc flags only —
    `--standalone`, `--toc`, `--number-sections`, `--self-contained`. Anything
    else → `err(...)`.
- **Returns:**
  ```json
  { "status": "success", "exit_code": 0, "stdout": "...", "stderr": "...", "output_path": "out.md" }
  ```
- **Notes:** pandoc subprocess; errors returned, never panics.
  **`availability()` requires pandoc only** — not pdflatex (old bug: the tool was
  hidden entirely when a LaTeX engine was missing even for non-pdf conversions).
- **Permission prompt:** `Convert {input_path} → {output_path}`.

---

## web_search
- **Permission:** readonly
- **Description:** Search the web via Tavily and return titles, URLs, and snippets.
  Use for anything that may have changed since training: docs, errors, package
  versions. Follow up interesting URLs with `web_extract`.
- **Args:**
  - `query` (required, string): the search query; be specific (versions, exact
    error text). Never append "current year" — use `datetime` first.
  - `max_results` (optional, integer, default 5, max 10).
- **Returns:**
  ```json
  { "status": "success", "query": "...", "results": [ { "title": "...", "url": "...", "content": "..." } ] }
  ```
- **Notes:** POST to `https://api.tavily.com/search` with a **shared static
  `reqwest::Client`** (connection reuse; the old code built a client per call).
  Consistent default (`5`) in schema, summary, and execution (the old code had
  5-or-10 drift). Parse the API response defensively — an error payload (rate
  limit, bad key) is `err(...)`, never a panic. Also mirror the result URLs to the
  TUI via `tool_output`.
- **`availability()`:** `TAVILY_API_KEY` set.

---

## web_extract
- **Permission:** readonly
- **Description:** Fetch the full readable content of a specific URL via Tavily.
  Use when a URL is known and its full content is needed (docs pages, READMEs,
  changelogs). More thorough than `web_search` snippets.
- **Args:** `url` (required, string).
- **Returns:** `{ "status": "success", "url": "...", "content": { ... } }`
  (content mirrors the Tavily extract response).
- **Notes:** POST to `https://api.tavily.com/extract` with the shared static
  client. Missing URL arg and API error payloads are `err(...)` (the old code
  panicked on both). Mirror extracted text to the TUI via `tool_output` for parity
  with `web_search`.
- **`availability()`:** `TAVILY_API_KEY` set.

---

## notify
- **Permission:** readonly
- **Description:** Send a desktop system notification to the user. Use when the
  user should be alerted outside the terminal: a long-running task finished, a
  build passed/failed after minutes, or Mia needs input and the user may be away.
  **Do not** notify on every tool result — only for things worth interrupting.
- **Args:**
  - `message` (required, string): the notification body text.
  - `title` (optional, string, default "Mia"): notification title.
  - `urgency` (optional, string, default "normal"): `"low" | "normal" | "critical"`
    (Linux only; ignored on macOS/Windows).
- **Returns:** `{ "status": "success", "channel": "notify-send" }`
- **Notes:**
  - Fire-and-forget: spawn, don't block on the user interacting with it.
  - Platform backends (spawn, don't embed):
    - Linux: `notify-send -a Mia -u <urgency> "<title>" "<message>"`.
    - macOS: `osascript -e 'display notification "<message>" with title "<title>"'`.
    - Windows: PowerShell toast via the BurntToast module
      (`New-BurntToastNotification`); documented prerequisite.
  - **Why readonly:** the whole point is to reach the user when they are *not*
    watching the TUI — a permission prompt would block on an absent user. This
    makes `notify` the one tool with a real side effect that never prompts;
    the `ReadOnly` class here means "no permission prompt required", not
    "zero side effects".
  - Spawn failure / missing backend → `err(...)` with the platform message.
- **`availability()`:** per platform — Linux: `notify-send` present; macOS:
  `osascript` present; Windows: `powershell` present.

---

## memory
- **Permission:** write
- **Description:** Insert or delete a single fact in persistent memory files.
  Two scopes:
  - `user`: facts about the user — identity, preferences, behaviour.
  - `system`: facts about the system/config and how to use tools effectively.
  Memory is included in every system prompt: keep entries terse and durable.
  Insert facts that stay relevant across sessions; delete facts that become wrong.
- **Args:**
  - `scope` (required, string): `"user" | "system"`.
  - `operation` (required, string): `"insert" | "delete"`.
  - `content` (required, string): the fact. Must be a single line (no `\n`/`\r`).
- **Returns:**
  ```json
  { "status": "success", "scope": "user", "operation": "insert", "path": "~/.local/share/mia/memory/user.txt", "message": "Line inserted successfully" }
  ```
- **Notes / algorithm:**
  1. Resolve the file from `AppConfig::internal().user_memory_file` /
     `system_memory_file` (paths already exist in config).
  2. Validate scope/operation enums and single-line content → else `err(...)`.
  3. Format: **one fact per line** (the old `§`-separator scheme is gone; newlines
     in facts are rejected).
  4. `insert`: skip if the exact line already exists (dedupe), else append.
  5. `delete`: remove all lines equal to `content`; nothing to delete is not an
     error (report it).
  6. All fs errors are `err(...)` with the io message — never `expect`/panic
     (fixes the old panics).
- **Permission prompt:** `Update memory` + `+ fact` / `− fact`.

---

# Implementation order

1. `datetime` — reference implementation exercising the full Tool trait. ✅
2. `memory` — simplest write tool; mirrors old logic minus panics/`§` format. ✅
3. `fs_read_file` — the chunked-read semantics worth getting right early. ✅
4. `fs_write_file`, `fs_list_dir`, `fs_tree`. ✅
5. `fs_file_ops`, `fs_edit_file` (the only tool with real matching logic). ✅
6. `fs_search_files`, `fs_search_dirs` (binary subprocess wrappers). ✅
7. `exec_shell` + `exec_python` (shared async runner, timeout, cancel). ✅
8. `notify` (platform spawn backends). ✅
9. `doc_create`, `doc_convert`. ✅
10. `web_search`, `web_extract` (static client). ✅
